title: Passive lumbar torso torque-angle in flexion, extension, axial twist (CW/CCW) and right/left lateral bend: exponential fits, males and females
levels: lumbar (rib cage/xiphoid relative to pelvis; moment about ~L4/L5)
condition: relaxed (EMG biofeedback), normal breathing, no belt

quantity.name: applied torque vs lumbar torso angle
quantity.definition: least-squares fit T = lambda*exp(beta*alpha) to the mean of the raw torque-angle data per sex and direction, fitted from 0 Nm to the torque still tolerated by half the subjects; T = applied torque about ~L4/L5 (Nm), alpha = rib cage-pelvis angle (deg) from the relaxed lying (flexion/extension, lateral bend) or standing (axial twist) start posture. Stiffness dT/dalpha = lambda*beta*exp(beta*alpha) (Nm/deg). Torque points at 4-deg steps are computed from the fits (derived)

source.authors: McGill S, Seguin J, Bennett G
source.sample: 22 male + 15 female undergraduates, no disabling LBP in the previous year

protocol.summary: Flexion/extension: side-lying; lateral bend: supine. Pelvis and lower body strapped to a fixed jig, upper torso (top of head to ~T12) strapped in a 'floating' cradle on precision nylon ball bearings over glass (no resistance to planar translation/rotation); scissor jacks aligned the spine in neutral, foam cushions under waist/knees when needed. Bending moment applied to the cradle by a cable kept normal to the cradle (load cell); moment = force x perpendicular distance to the lateral iliac crest (~L4/L5). Axial rotation: upright standing, rib cage fixed by a restraining harness, torque applied to a rotating platform under the feet. Angle = rib cage (3-SPACE Isotrak sensor over xiphoid) relative to pelvis (source strapped to pelvis), accuracy +-0.3 deg. Audio EMG biofeedback (bilateral L3 erector spinae and external oblique) to relax; trials with prolonged EMG repeated. Torque ramped over ~10 s (peak at 7-8 s) until the subject's tolerance limit. 3 trials x 6 directions (flexion, extension, CW twist, CCW twist, right and left lateral bend) x 3 conditions (normal, held breath at maximal inhalation, leather lifting belt 11 cm posterior / 6.5 cm anterior); condition order fixed (normal, breath hold, belt). Mean raw torque-angle data per sex, direction and condition fitted with T = lambda*exp(beta*alpha) (T in Nm, alpha in deg) from 0 Nm up to the torque still tolerated by half the subjects.
how_to_simulate: Flexion/extension: side-lying; lateral bend: supine; pelvis and lower body fixed, upper torso (to ~T12) on a frictionless cradle (no gravity moment in the bending plane, no compressive preload)
Axial twist: upright standing, rib cage fixed, pelvis/lower body rotated about the vertical axis
Set all muscle activations to zero (passive tissues and passive muscle only); no belt, normal breathing
Impose rib cage-to-pelvis rotation in each of the six directions in steps up to the fitted range (data[].note) and compute the passive resisting moment about L4/L5
Compare torque at each angle with the sex-matched fitted curve; compare stiffness dT/dalpha

subject_model.source: Table 1 male means (female cohort: 20.8 y, 164.8 cm, 62.3 kg)

protocol.notes: Fits pass through T = lambda (1.2-2.4 Nm) at alpha = 0, not 0 Nm: the fitted exponential does not describe the toe region near neutral, so compare from ~4 deg on. No between-subject SD or fit error reported (Fig 2 shows large inter-subject scatter: at 30 deg extension torques span ~10-30 Nm). The fitted range differs by direction: Fig 3 plots the fits to 10 Nm (flexion, extension, CCW), 8 Nm (CW) and 18 Nm (lateral bend); Table 4 lists male normal values to 16/22/24/20 deg (flexion/extension/CW/R lateral bend). Fig 4 50%-participation torques (digitised) are higher than these plotted ranges (e.g. extension ~16 Nm vs 10 Nm), so the derived points stop at the more conservative limit. CW/CCW are the twist directions as labelled in the paper (torque applied at the feet with the rib cage fixed); the paper does not map them to left/right trunk rotation. Gender differences in curve shape significant for CW twist-normal (GLM).

extraction.from: Table 1 (p.697, subjects), Table 3 (p.701, coefficients), Fig 3 (p.700, fitted torque ranges), Fig 4 (p.702, participation curves)
extraction.uncertainty: coefficients as printed (2 decimals; beta rounding to 0.01 alone changes T by up to ~20% at 20 deg); Fig 4 50% torques +-0.5 Nm; Fig 4 min/max +-1 Nm
extraction.check_notes: Scanned PDF (no text layer): Table 3 re-read from a 300 dpi render. Consistency check: Table 4 k recomputed from Table 3 male normal coefficients (flexion 2 deg: 2.12*0.11*e^0.22 = 0.29 = printed 0.29; extension 2 deg: 0.166 vs 0.17) - Table 4 was computed with unrounded beta. Fig 4 digitised on the 300 dpi render by reading the normal (solid, unmarked) line at the bracketing 2-Nm ticks and interpolating linearly to 50% (flexion 54.7% at 12 Nm / 32% at 14 Nm; extension ~48% at 16 Nm; CW 55% at 10 Nm / 37% at 12 Nm; R bend ~50% at 28 Nm). Only male participation curves (4 directions) are printed; female and CCW / L bend not shown.

pass_rule.rule: model passive torque within +-25% of the sex-matched fitted curve between 4 deg and the fitted range limit (no SD reported); torque-angle curve monotonically stiffening in every direction
